jobs.title: Deputy Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.excerpt: Together for Girls works around the world and combines state-of-the-art data with powerful advocacy to end violence against children and adolescents, especially sexual violence.
jobs.description:
Together for Girls works around the world and combines state-of-the-art data with powerful advocacy to end violence against children and adolescents, especially sexual violence. Through data and advocacy, TfG drives action to break cycles of violence and ensure prevention, healing, and justice. By connecting the dots between understanding the problem, identifying effective solutions, tracking progress, and mobilizing for action, TfG creates a synergistic effect that amplifies its impact and drives toward its ultimate goal of creating a safer world for children and adolescents.

Grounded in 19 years of data from the Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS), which provide a clear picture of the problem, we drive coordinated action through three initiatives that collectively contribute to ending violence against children. The Safe Futures Solutions Hub shares evidence and practice-based knowledge to inform effective prevention and response efforts, ensuring access to proven solutions across sectors. The Brave Movement mobilizes survivors and allies worldwide to drive political will, influence policy, and ensure that inaction is not an option. Finally, the Out of the Shadows Index tracks countries’ progress in addressing violence, providing an accountability framework and benchmark for advocacy. Together, these initiatives form a powerful model that transforms evidence into collective action for prevention, healing, and justice.

We are a nimble and highly impactful team that continues to grow and evolve. We work with a broad range of organizations, researchers, and advocates to drive change.

Position Overview

The Deputy Director, Financial Planning & Analysis plays a key role in strengthening Together for Girls’ financial planning, analysis, and grant financial management across its US and European entities. Reporting to the Senior Director, Finance, this role leads and supports budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis, grant financial management, and proposal costing, translating complex financial information into clear insights that support organizational decision-making.

Working closely with Finance, Development, Grants Management, and Program teams, the Deputy Director, Financial Planning & Analysis will help ensure TfG effectively plans and manages resources across a diverse portfolio of donor-funded programs. The role requires both strong technical financial skills and the ability to partner with non-finance colleagues, identify emerging financial risks and opportunities, and develop practical tools and analysis that strengthen financial management across the organization.

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Partner with the Senior Director of Finance to develop and maintain annual organizational budgets across TfG’s US and European entities, coordinate periodic re-forecasts, and strengthen organization-wide budgeting and planning tools.
  • Produce consolidated financial analysis and reporting, including quarterly budget-to-actual variance analysis, forecasts, financial health metrics, and other insights to support management and leadership decision-making.
  • Develop financial models and scenario analyses to inform organizational planning, new initiatives, funding opportunities, cost structures, and the continued development of TfG’s multi-entity operating model.
  • Working closely with the Senior Manager of Finance & Operations, manage financial planning and analysis for an assigned portfolio of grants, including monitoring burn rates, forecasting expenditures, reconciling financial activity to the general ledger, and preparing accurate donor financial reports.
  • Partner with program and project management teams to strengthen grant forecasting and ensure financial plans reflect anticipated program delivery, staffing, and award timelines.
  • Maintain and analyze staff level-of-effort (LOE) allocations across grants, entities, fiscal years, and award periods; monitor actual and budgeted effort and identify funding gaps, over- or under-allocation, and other emerging risks.
  • Reconcile LOE and personnel costs against payroll allocations and grant budgets and provide analysis to support re-forecasting, proposal development, effort reporting, audit requirements, and applicable cost-recharge methodologies based on donor expectations.
  • Lead financial modeling and budget development for new proposals, working with Finance, Development, Programs, and Grants Management to develop funder-ready budgets, model staffing and other cost assumptions, and ensure alignment with donor cost requirements and organizational financial targets.
  • Support effective indirect cost recovery and broader cost-allocation approaches across TfG’s diverse funding portfolio, contributing financial analysis to discussions about donor requirements and organizational cost structures.
  • Partner closely with the Grants & Compliance Manager, Senior Manager Finance & Operations and other colleagues to ensure financial reporting and grant management are accurate, timely, and aligned with applicable donor requirements.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of financial systems, models, templates, dashboards, and processes to strengthen efficiency, accuracy, visibility, and financial decision-making across the organization.
  • Other duties, as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills and Experience:

  • 5–8 years of progressively responsible experience in nonprofit/NGO finance, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), grants finance, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex organizational and/or grant budgets, forecasting, financial analysis, and budget-to-actual reporting.
  • Strong knowledge of grant and fund accounting principles and experience managing finances across a diverse donor-funded portfolio.
  • Experience with financial requirements and reporting for institutional donors; experience with government, bilateral, multilateral, and/or foundation funders such as the European Union, FCDO, Global Affairs Canada, or similar donors strongly preferred.
  • Advanced Excel skills and demonstrated ability to develop and maintain financial models, forecasts, allocation methodologies, and analytical tools.
  • Experience working with accounting and financial management systems, including QuickBooks and/or other ERP or customized financial systems.
  • Strong analytical judgment and ability to identify financial trends, risks, and opportunities and translate complex financial information into clear, actionable insights for non-finance audiences.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to financial accuracy, combined with the ability to understand the broader organizational and programmatic implications of financial information.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex workstreams, deadlines, grants, and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with experience partnering effectively with program, development, grants, operations, and senior leadership colleagues.
  • Experience working across multiple legal entities, currencies, or international operations preferred.
  • Experience with personnel cost allocation, level-of-effort tracking, indirect cost recovery, and/or donor effort-reporting requirements preferred.
  • Comfortable working independently in a globally distributed, cross-functional environment and exercising sound judgment within established organizational and financial frameworks.
  • Alignment with the mission and values of Together for Girls.

Location & Ways of Working

This position is a full-time position that must be based in the United States or United Kingdom. Applicants should have work authorization for their preferred location.

This is a remote position with the expectation to travel to attend in-person meetings and events. This position will also require travel up to 10%.

All team members are expected to be available during Together for Girls’ core working hours of 8:00 AM - 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. The other four hours that the team member chooses to work are flexible and may be coordinated with their supervisor.

Compensation

This role offers a competitive salary adjusted to the cost of labor in the city where the candidate resides. Final salary within this location adjusted range will also be determined by the candidate’s qualifications and years and type of experience.

For example, the annual salary for the position for a candidate based in:

  • Washington, DC will be $97,000 - $113,000
  • Boston, MA will be $111,000 - $127,000
  • London, United Kingdom will be £72,800 - £83,400

Together for Girls offers competitive pay, paid leave, and comprehensive health insurance. Specific benefits vary by country.

Culture and Values

Together for Girls seeks to create a courageous, inclusive, and flexible culture that empowers our staff to have the capacity and ability to deliver change. We strive to build and maintain psychological safety, trust, and accountability among team members in order to foster honesty and openness about our needs and challenges while also prioritizing self-care. We are a rapidly expanding organization that requires staff to be nimble and flexible, comfortable with uncertainty and able to adapt in real time to emerging opportunities.

Brave Movement Applicants

We warmly encourage members of the Brave Movement to apply. While membership is not a requirement for this role, we value the lived experience, leadership, and commitment that members bring to advancing survivor-centered advocacy and strengthening our global movement.

Application Information

Together for Girls, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer and committed to maintaining an inclusive and diverse working environment free from discrimination and harassment. Qualified applicants from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Together for Girls, Inc. is a registered 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in the U.S.

jobs.description:
Interim Managing Director

California Coalition for Worker Power (CCWP)
Housed at Koreatown Immigrant Workers Alliance (KIWA)

About CCWP

The California Coalition for Worker Power (CCWP) is a statewide table of worker centers, labor policy advocates, and unions advancing strategies that build durable worker power across California. Our coalition focuses on structural reforms that strengthen worker organizations, expand collective voice, and protect workers, including immigrant and Black workers, from retaliation and exploitation.California Coalition for Worker Power seeks an Interim Managing Director who understands coalition dynamics, coalition tables, operational systems and finances and can work collaboratively with CCWP leadership team, staff, and partners.

Overview

  • Position Type: At-will, temporary, exempt
  • Location: Remote, must be California-based
  • Duration: 6-18 months
  • Reports To: KIWA’s Executive Director, Coalition Co-Presidents and Co-Managing Directors

Position Summary

California Coalition for Worker Power seeks an experienced and hands-on Interim Managing Director to provide financial leadership and operational support during a short-term transition period. The Interim Managing Director will set up systems and oversee the organization’s financial operations, strengthen organizational digital security protocols, partner with the leadership team to fundraise strategy, and provide oversight of organizational activities, priorities, projects and decisions.

The ideal candidate is a proven operations and executive leader who can quickly create unified finance systems, oversee priorities, and work effectively with directors, staff, finance, and coalition partners to execute plans.

Job Description

We are seeking a proven and experienced Interim Managing Director who will provide strategic and operational leadership to set up systems to the coalition’s continued growth, effectiveness, and alignment during a period of transition. Working closely with coalition leadership, staff, and member organizations, the Interim Managing Director will create and strengthen internal systems, facilitate cross-coalition coordination, and ensure that organizational priorities are translated into clear plans and effective execution.

The Interim Managing Director will partner with CCWP leadership and workgroups to lead the following areas:

Finance & Administration

  • Working with coalition leadership, drive a process to consolidate the coalition’s organizational structure, including transition to a single fiscal entity.
  • Oversee the completion of the coalition’s financial systems, including identifying gaps and implementing practical systems to improve financial visibility, accountability, compliance and decision-making.
  • Lead and oversee the 2027 budget process and subgrants process including the development of overall strategy, support decision-making regarding overall budget and subgrant amounts, coordinate with staff, manage disbursements, and ensure appropriate financial documentation and accountability
  • Work with all relevant parties to ensure compliance with coalition’s financial policies and procedures, as well as applicable grant requirements, accounting standards, and other financial obligations
  • Monitor budget-to-actual performance, identify trends, variances and potential areas of over- or underspending and proactively collaborate with staff and leadership team.
  • Support the development and implementation of organizational security protocols.

Organizational Operations

  • Lead the day-to-day operations of the coalition; ensure that decision-making structures, roles, responsibilities, and processes are clear, effective, and aligned with the coalition's long term agenda and goals.
  • Ensure continuity between coalition meetings and decision-making spaces, communicate decisions, next steps, ownership, and timelines so that collective work moves forward between convenings, and retreats.
  • Serve as strategic thought partner to coalition leadership, help navigate competing priorities, resolve organizational and governance challenges, and maintain focus on shared goals.
  • Maintain clear governance documentation, include decisions, policies, roles, meeting records, workplans, and other materials necessary to support institutional memory and accountability.
  • Evaluate and strengthen coalition governance practices over time, use feedback and experience to improve how the coalition makes decisions, shares power, manages conflict, and advances collective work.

Leadership Support

  • Coordinate and facilitate staff and Leadership team meetings including develop agendas, sequence and prioritize topics, manage scheduling, and ensure clear decisions and next stepsPlan and coordinate Leadership Team and Coordinating Committee retreats, ensuring clear objects, effective agendas, strong facilitation, and alignment with organizational priorities
  • Provide strategic oversight of organizational priorities, ensuring that key initiatives, projects, and meetings remain focused on the coalition’s measurable outcomes, and long term vision..
  • Track organizational commitments, priorities and deliverables, proactively identifying potential delays, competing demands or capacity challenges and sounding the alarm when commitments or timelines are at risk

Job Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a strategic, systems-oriented leader who brings strong attention to detail while maintaining a clear understanding of the organization’s broader goals and mission. They are comfortable operating in complex, fast-moving environments and have the ability to translate strategy into effective systems, processes, and action.

The successful candidate will have:

  • Strong systems thinking and attention to detail, with the ability to see the big picture, connect across functions, and build practical systems that support organizational effectiveness.
  • Strong project and program management skills, including the ability to develop plans, establish timelines, coordinate stakeholders, and ensure projects move from strategy to completion.
  • The ability to thrive in complexity, manage competing priorities, and exercise sound judgment in a dynamic, mission-driven environment.
  • Familiarity with financial systems and tools, including QuickBooks, Bill.com, and related nonprofit financial management systems.
  • Understanding of nonprofit organizational structures and organizational development and security, with an appreciation for the systems, processes, and culture needed to support a healthy and effective organization.
  • Experience with coalition-based work, including the ability to build relationships, coordinate across diverse stakeholders, follow through on commitments, and help groups move from discussion to action.
  • Familiarity with the California labor movement, including an understanding of its organizations, stakeholders, priorities, and organizing and coalition-building approaches.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build trust, create accountability, and move work forward across teams and organizations.
  • A proactive, solutions-oriented approach, with the ability to identify what needs to happen, bring the right people together, and follow through to get it done.
  • Being bilingual in Spanish is a plus.

Compensation and Benefits

Salary: $135,000 to $150,000 annual, to be negotiated based on experience and scope.

Benefits: Employee healthcare, dental and vision plan; PTO and paid holidays; 403b retirement plan

Supervision & Collaboration Structure

The Interim Managing Director will:

  • Report to the Executive Director of Koreatown Immigrant Workers Alliance (KIWA), who also serves as CCWP Co-President.
  • Coordinate closely with CCWP’s Co-Managing Directors and staff to ensure effective organizational coordination and alignment.
  • Work in close partnership with CCWP’s steering committee, policy, organizing, and communications workgroups to align legislative strategy, coalition organizing, and public engagement.

Equity Commitment

KIWA is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, religion, color, sex, disability, sexual orientation or national origin. Candidates whose backgrounds, identities, and/or lived experience have been historically marginalized in roles like this are strongly encouraged to apply.

Application Requirements

Please submit:

  1. Resume
  2. A brief cover letter highlighting a proven track record of successfully establishing and leading scalable operations or equivalent in a growing nonprofit, coalition, or community-based organization.
  3. Three professional references

If you are interested, apply above.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Salary: $135,000 to $150,000

jobs.title: Software Engineer (Frontend)
jobs.excerpt: Metabase is the easiest way for people to get insights from their data, from tiny startups who get up and running quickly to major corporations with tens of thousands of users.
jobs.description:
Metabase is the easiest way for people to get insights from their data, from tiny startups who get up and running quickly to major corporations with tens of thousands of users. That's why people love us.
We bring data tools with the elegance and simplicity of consumer products to the crufty world of enterprise business intelligence. We provide an opinionated open source starting point for how companies should measure, analyze and share their data, which is used by tens of thousands of companies.
We built Metabase because existing tools for business intelligence didn’t feel like things we wanted to use. We wanted faster, simpler ways to ask questions about data, and wanted to strip away the colder feel of most Enterprise software. Folks seemed to agree, and now Metabase is used daily by tens of thousands of companies to give people in all sorts of roles access to insights they wouldn’t have otherwise had. None of this could happen without our user interface and that’s where you come in. We’re looking for someone with strong product sensibilities, extraordinarily good frontend skills, and solid software engineering fundamentals to join our team to advance the state of the art in our product and our industry.
We are hiring for multiple frontend software engineer positions.

Why choose Metabase

  • The problems we face are genuinely interesting and aren’t trivial. Data influences so much of our world but isn’t that easy to interact with or understand. You’ll make tools that people rely on for their real jobs.
  • You’ll get to work in open source and get feedback directly from users and customers out in the open.
  • The company is growing and so is the business. We’re adding new remote team members from around the world and improving our processes. It’s an exciting time and you can really have an impact on how things work here.
  • We’ve tried to design our work environment to fit into real life. Work is only one part of who you are, so we emphasize reasonable workdays and prefer planning and avoiding panic. People at Metabase have families, dogs, plants, and lives outside of work and we try to support that however we can.

What we're looking for

  • You care about crafting delightful user experiences. You like to write code to enable people to do something and you understand that details and things like copy matter. If your focus is only on code this might not be the best role for you.
  • Prior experience shipping non-trivial apps using React + Redux (or equivalent). Our front end is written in React (surprise!), so you’ll need really strong React and JavaScript knowledge to build fast and thoughtful user interfaces.
  • You have experience writing tests, giving good feedback on other people’s code, and writing proposals for more complicated problems that are thoughtful and clear. As we’re a remote company (even outside of pandemics) communication and clarity are really important.
  • Due to the nature of what we work on, computer science-y problems come up frequently. We’re not picky about a specific degree or accolade, but you’ll be expected to write fast and performant code and deal with a fair bit of data structure manipulation regularly.
  • We like everyone to care about the nuts and bolts of how to make things look good, so you’ll be expected to use our style guide and if necessary write or update our CSS, so comfort in CSS and familiarity with things like design systems and component libraries is a necessity.
  • You’ve worked on a large and complex JavaScript project. Metabase is a big product and code base so the ability to adapt existing code and integrate new code into established systems is important and you should feel comfortable digging in.

Not essential, but nice to have

  • Knowledge and prior experience with data visualization (especially if it has involved dc.js and d3.js).
  • Previous contributions to open source (not a requirement, but a huge plus).
  • Either pre-existing knowledge or interest in learning some Clojure, the language much of the backend of our application is written in.

The types of problems you'd get to work on

  • Lightning fast interaction with data. Think things like letting people see all the orders that came in from a specific region by clicking directly on a custom map of their sales regions and then letting them filter that list visually by directly interacting with the data table - and all of this happening in a responsive and delightful way.
  • Augmenting visualizations. To allow for people to further institutional knowledge, build the feature to allow annotations directly on specific data points in a line chart, and then determine how to expose those when it makes sense across dashboards and the entire app.
  • Wayfinding. We want to make sure people don’t have to do work that’s already been done, so build new ways to surface important metrics or segments to the right users across Metabase.
  • Embedded analytics. We have customers who deliver analytics to their own users via our embed product. You’d get to tackle the problem of making sure those can match their own products visually and enable easier integration of the embeds into their own code.
Compensation
The US base salary range for this role is $110K–$210K annually, plus equity and benefits.
Compensation is determined by role, level, location, and individual qualifications, including skills, experience, and scope of responsibility. Pay may vary by geographic location and other job-related factors.

Benefits
We offer meaningful equity and a comprehensive US benefits package, including fully employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance (with 75% coverage for dependents), a 401(k) with employer match available to enroll after the first 30 days, flexible and unlimited paid time off including sick time, and an asynchronous, remote-first environment.
We're a global team (50% outside the US), fully distributed (from Thailand to California), who get things done asynchronously, with plenty of uninterrupted time, supporting each other to do the best work of our careers. We offer flexibility (define your own schedule and work from wherever you want), autonomy, and an environment that fosters growth, learning, and development. We're relentlessly user-focused and believe in building long-term value, not short-term hacks. And we raised a $30M Series B to take our approach to the next level for years to come.

Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.
The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role:

addons.mozilla.org (AMO) is the foundation of the Firefox add-ons ecosystem. It’s a showcase for developers to publish and grow their extensions, and a place of discovery for millions of users who customize Firefox to make it their own. Behind the scenes are the DevHub which enables developers to manage their extensions. To manage the ecosystem there are a series of Reviewer tools and automated moderation systems.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll bring a passion for crafting resilient systems that accelerate our review and moderation teams to provide a first-class experience for Add-on developers. You’ll work closely with engineers, reviewers, developer support, and Add-ons leadership to turn ideas into polished features, modernize the platform and its architecture, and see your work reach millions of people around the world.


What you’ll do:
  • Deliver major features and architectural improvements across the Add-ons stack, including automated moderation pipelines, Reviewer tools, and DevHub.
  • Help establish and maintain engineering standards across areas such as code review, definition of done, production readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call practices, coding conventions, and infrastructure as code.
  • Create robust observability systems and data-backed insights.
  • Provide peer feedback, share knowledge and help others grow.
  • Build and improve the systems that enable Add-ons engineering to safely develop, deploy, observe, and operate production services.
  • Improve our CI/CD pipelines using declarative, pipeline-as-code approaches that make changes reproducible, testable, and easy to review.
  • Deliver work iteratively using a visible backlog, short feedback cycles, retrospectives, and demonstrations to stakeholders.
  • Write clear technical documentation, including design notes, Architecture Decision Records, runbooks, and incident write-ups.
  • Work effectively in unfamiliar codebases, tracing requests and asynchronous jobs end-to-end to understand failures and identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Contribute in the open through pull requests, code reviews, and discussions.
  • Work on:

    • AMO application systems: Work within our Python/Django, MySQL, React/TypeScript, and asynchronous processing systems.
    • Internal developer platforms: Create tools and paved paths that make it easier for teams to ship and operate software safely and consistently.
    • Team Process: Contribute to team ceremonies, execute process improvement, and provide feedback on team effectiveness.
    • Engineering standards: Help make production readiness, testing, recoverability, documentation, and safe deployment part of the normal development lifecycle.
    • Platform reliability: Deployments, monitoring, and incident response.

What you’ll bring:

  • Strong hands-on experience building and maintaining production applications with Python/Django.
  • Experience operating and improving production software systems where reliability and safe delivery matter.
  • Strong experience with CI/CD systems and treating pipelines and infrastructure declaratively as code.
  • Experience designing or improving automated testing and deployment workflows, including integration testing and staged or progressive delivery.
  • Strong understanding of observability as an engineering discipline, including metrics, logging, tracing, service-level objectives, and actionable alerting.
  • Experience building or maintaining internal tools or platforms used by other engineering teams, with an understanding that internal systems have users, reliability expectations, roadmaps, and lifecycle considerations.
  • Experience defining or improving engineering practices such as code review standards, operational readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call expectations, or definitions of done.
  • Ability to read and understand unfamiliar codebases and trace application behavior across frontend, backend, asynchronous jobs, data stores, and infrastructure.
  • Experience debugging complex production issues and turning what you learn into lasting system improvements.
  • Strong technical writing skills, with experience creating useful documentation such as design documents, ADRs, runbooks, and incident reports.
  • Experience working iteratively with a visible backlog, regular stakeholder feedback, and retrospectives that result in concrete improvements.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in a distributed team environment.
  • A willingness to share knowledge and mentor peers in operational and reliability practices.
  • Commitment to our values:
    • Welcoming differences
    • Being relationship-minded
    • Practicing responsible participation
    • Having grit

Bonus points for:

  • Experience with Google Cloud and operating Kubernetes.
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code tooling and policy-as-code.
  • Experience establishing SLOs and error-budget-based reliability practices.
  • Experience with chaos engineering, disaster recovery testing, or production readiness reviews.
  • Experience with trust and safety, automated moderation, abuse prevention, or other adversarial systems.
  • Contributions to open source projects

When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Grants Associate Job Announcement

Heartland Fund is seeking a Grants Associate. For a thoughtful, mission-driven professional, this position is an exciting opportunity to support new systems and processes in a rapidly growing grantmaking organization and ever changing compliance environment.

Heartland Fund’s Grants Associate supports the organization’s grants management cycle, with a focus on grants management system support, record maintenance, documentation tracking, reporting, and coordination throughout the grantmaking cycle. This role helps ensure grantmaking activities run smoothly, records are accurate and up to date, and staff and grantees receive timely and effective support. The successful candidate will be detail-oriented, responsive, and able to manage multiple responsibilities while working collaboratively with internal teams and external partners.

You will have an opportunity to help us enable equitable investment in rural communities, democracy, and climate solutions. This is a unique and dynamic position with opportunities for growth and impact as the Heartland Fund prepares to launch as an independent entity in 2027.

This is a remote position with a salary range of $59,500 - $70,000 and includes a generous benefits package.

About the Organization

As a funder collaborative, the Heartland Fund scales investment, supports local leaders, and builds long-term partnerships with rural and Native organizations to create thriving places where rural working people can determine our own futures, strengthening the entire nation. Heartland's grantmaking and programmatic investments support rural people working to transform their lives and communities toward shared prosperity, a healthy climate, and stronger democracy. We invest in building local capacity for issue advocacy, community organizing, economic development and local jobs, climate solutions, civic engagement, and sustainable urban-rural coalitions. We prioritize racial justice in all aspects of our work. In addition to grantmaking, Heartland also supports rural leaders and organizations through convening, research, and communications and storytelling.

Heartland Fund has three programs:

  • Rural Democracy expands nonpartisan civic participation and counters policies that harm our democratic institutions in places where rural action can define policy and democratic outcomes.

  • Resource Rural (RR) mobilizes resources enabling rural communities to unlock public and private investment to create positive economic change in their communities.

  • Rural Climate Partnership (RCP) supports hometowns across America to accelerate climate solutions and build healthy local economies.

Both RR and RCP programs help rural communities access public funding – through place-based technical assistance, local organizing, and a large-scale communications and narrative effort – to make a tangible difference in rural people’s lives and to advance climate mitigation and resilience.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities

The Grants Associate works closely with the grants management team, program staff, grantees, and external partners to support effective grantmaking operations. This role is responsible for maintaining grant records, supporting the grants management system, gathering and tracking required documentation, and helping ensure grants management processes and timelines are carried out accurately and efficiently.

Grants Administration

  • Support grantees and internal teams throughout the grants management cycle - from invitation through final close out.

  • Create new and update existing contact, organization, and grant accounts and records, as needed.

  • Track and follow up on narrative and financial reports and maintain other outstanding documentation.

  • Determine grantee organization eligibility and support due diligence process.

Grants Management Support

  • Serve as technical support to staff and grantees related to the Fluxx grants management system.

  • Assist in training staff and grantees on technology, policy issues, and procedures that affect their grants management work.

  • Develop templates & tools for recurring grants management activities and tasks.

  • Support grants management team coordination.

Team Coordination & Knowledge Management

  • Create dashboards and analyze reports on grant data for staff and external audiences.

  • Work proactively with the grants management team, program leads, and external partners to help ensure the grantmaking and reporting timelines stay on track.

  • Support staff team in preparing board, committee, and strategic partnerships materials, as needed.

  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as requested or assigned.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented, collaborative professional with at least three years of experience in grants management or a related philanthropic/nonprofit setting, who brings strong project coordination skills and comfort navigating complex, multi-stakeholder workflows. They can balance meticulous record-keeping with proactive communication to keep grantees and internal teams on track.

Heartland Fund’s growing team takes pride in building an organizational culture rooted in learning, collaboration, racial justice, and a deep commitment to our mission. All staff are expected to provide leadership and vision to advance our mission, vision, and core strategies.

Qualifications

We realize that some great candidates may not have every single thing on this list. If you believe you would be a great fit for this role, we encourage you to apply.

Essential

  • Minimum of three years professional experience, including some nonprofit experience.

  • Strong proficiency with Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Drive) and video conferencing platforms (Zoom, etc.)

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

  • Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills

  • Strong project management skills, and experience tracking, coordinating and helping complete complex collaborative projects

  • Highly collaborative with a partnership mindset

  • Entrepreneurial and resourceful, a proactive and creative problem-solver

  • Commitment to racial justice and equity

Desired

  • Experience in a philanthropic, fiscal sponsor, nonprofit intermediary, funder collaborative and/or other type of grantmaking organization (or equivalent)

  • Experience successfully operating in a start-up environment

  • Knowledge of Grants Management Systems and Processes (Fluxx Preferred)

  • Understanding of the financial and regulatory environment for nonprofit and philanthropic entities.

  • Demonstrated experience working effectively with colleagues of diverse backgrounds and perspectives:

    • Appreciation of the diverse cultural traditions of rural people and places

    • Comfort working with a range of individuals in nonprofit organizations, government, foundations, and private sectors

  • Working proficiency of a second language that is spoken in rural America

  • Experience living and/or working in rural America is strongly preferred.

Compensation & Job Design

This is a full-time, exempt position. The organization is virtual, and the position may work remotely from their home within the United States. The starting salary range for this position is $59,500 - $70,000.

The comprehensive beneﬁts package includes 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance for employees (and their families). Employees are able to enroll in a 401k retirement plan and are eligible for a 3% automatic contribution and up to a 3% employer match on 401k contributions. Employees are also eligible for pre-tax transportation beneﬁts. Full-time employees will receive 120 hours of vacation time, 80 hours of health leave, up to 2 days of casual leave, and 20 hours of volunteer leave annually. Employees will also receive 13 paid holidays throughout the calendar year. Employees are eligible for 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave after 90 days of employment. All employees of Windward are required to complete timesheets.

Heartland Fund is a project of Windward Fund, a 501(c)(3) public charity that incubates new and innovative public-interest projects and grant-making programs. Windward Fund is committed to attracting, developing and retaining exceptional people, and to creating a work environment that is dynamic, rewarding and enables each of us to realize our potential.

Windward Fund’s work environment is safe and open to all employees and partners, respecting the full spectrum of race, color, religious creed, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, political afﬁliation, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, and all other classiﬁcations protected by law in the locality and/or state in which you are working.

The individual holding this position will also work part-time for a coordinated project, Rural Victory Fund, in Sixteen Thirty Fund, a 501(c)(4) organization, under a resource-sharing agreement between Windward Fund and Sixteen Thirty Fund. The responsibilities under that position will be overseen by Sixteen Thirty Fund.

Windward participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with employees’ Form I-9 information to conﬁrm authorization to work in the United States. Job candidates and employees authorized to work may not be discriminated against on the basis of national origin or citizenship status.

Travel Requirements

This position requires occasional travel within the United States.

How to Apply

Applications will be reviewed and considered on a rolling basis. A limited number of screening calls and interview spots will be filled starting in September 2026, with a desired start date by November 2026. Early applications are strongly encouraged.

Company Overview:Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody. Our two primary products – BlinkRx and Quick Save – remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients.

BlinkRx is the world’s first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform. With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock.

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!

Hours: Full-time, salaried (40hrs/week), Mon-Fri, 7:30am-9pm ET rotating shifts and rotating Saturdays 7:00am-5pm ET

The Opportunity:

As a BlinkRx Pharmacist, you are the clinical backbone of our closed-door facility. You will verify prescriptions with speed and precision, provide proactive phone-based patient counseling, and collaborate with prescribers to keep medications moving without compromising safety. This role is ideal for pharmacists who thrive in a structured, high-throughput environment and are passionate about improving patient outcomes at scale.

Responsibilities:

Prescription Verification and Dispensing

  • Review and clinically verify new and refill prescriptions for therapeutic appropriateness, drug-drug interactions, contraindications, and dosing accuracy
  • Validate prescription data entry performed by pharmacy technicians, ensuring transcription accuracy from provider orders and transfer records
  • Perform pharmacist verification of filled prescriptions in a closed-door fulfillment environment, confirming accuracy of drug, dose, quantity, NDC, and labeling prior to release for shipment
  • Perform daily prospective drug utilization review (DUR) to identify and resolve clinical flags before fulfillment
  • Manage specialty medication handling requirements including cold-chain verification

Patient Care

All patient interaction at BlinkRx is conducted by phone or digital platforms. Our pharmacists are the primary clinical contact for patients and must deliver a high standard of care in every call.

  • Provide proactive outbound patient counseling calls for new prescriptions, addressing drug education, expected side effects, dosing instructions, storage requirements, and adherence strategies
  • Handle inbound clinical patient calls related to counseling and clinical inquiries, while directing non-clinical inquiries, such as refill status and delivery questions, to the patient support team.
  • Document all patient interactions thoroughly in the patient profile within the pharmacy management system
  • Support Spanish-speaking patients with bilingual counseling where applicable

Prescriber Collaboration and Clinical Outreach

  • Contact prescriber offices via phone and electronic messaging to clarify incomplete, ambiguous, or clinically inappropriate prescriptions prior to dispensing
  • Partner with prescribers on therapeutic substitutions, DAW overrides, and formulary alternatives to reduce dispensing delays

Pharmacy Technician Supervision and Workflow Management

  • Supervise pharmacy technicians across data entry, prescription processing, packaging, and fulfillment workflows in accordance with state board regulations and in collaboration with technician management
  • Conduct real-time quality checks on technician work product, providing immediate corrective feedback to maintain accuracy standards
  • Identify and escalate technician performance trends to pharmacy leadership; participate in coaching and training as directed

Compliance, Safety and Quality

  • Ensure strict compliance with HIPAA, state pharmacy practice acts, federal DEA regulations, and all BlinkRx corporate policies
  • Oversee proper handling, documentation, and destruction of PHI-containing records and materials in alignment with privacy protocols
  • Participate in quality assurance activities including internal audits, prescription error tracking, and near-miss reporting
  • Report adverse drug events and medication errors through established pharmacovigilance channels, when applicable
  • Maintain fulfillment area compliance standards, including proper storage of temperature-sensitive medications

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with pharmacy leadership, patient services, clinical, compliance, and technology teams to drive operational and clinical improvements
  • Coordinate with the shipping and fulfillment team to resolve packaging errors, return-to-sender issues, and delivery failures affecting patient medication access
  • Provide clinical input on technology enhancements, workflow tools, and software configurations that affect the pharmacist verification or patient counseling experience
  • Participate in team huddles, quality reviews, and department meetings to support continuous improvement initiatives

Qualifications:

Required

  • Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree from an ACPE-accredited College of Pharmacy
  • Active Missouri Pharmacy License in good standing with the Missouri Board of Pharmacy
  • Strong command of the English language (written and verbal); bilingual Spanish preferred for phone-based patient counseling
  • Demonstrated ability to perform high-volume prescription verification with strong attention to detail and accuracy
  • Strong technical aptitude and ability to learn pharmacy management systems, verification platforms, and internal workflow tools

Preferred

  • 3+ years of experience in a mail order, specialty, retail or closed-door fulfillment pharmacy
  • Active pharmacy licensure required in home state; candidates must obtain licensure in 3 additional states from the list below within the first 9 months of hire (prior licensure in any of the following states is a plus):
    • AK, AL, AR, CA, ID, IL, KS, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MS, NE, NV, OK, OR, TN, TX, VA, WV
  • Familiarity with pharmacovigilance or adverse drug event reporting protocols

What Success Looks Like:

  • Prescription verification queues are processed accurately and on time without sacrificing clinical quality
  • Every patient who receives a counseling call feels informed, supported, and confident in their therapy
  • Prescriber outreach is proactive and efficient, minimizing dispensing delays caused by incomplete or unclear orders
  • Compliance and quality standards are upheld without exception in a fast-paced environment
  • You are a trusted clinical partner within the BlinkRx team — shaping the patient experience from behind the scenes

At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. We are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year. Our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company. We are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers.

Na Spassu, estamos com um projeto incrível no ar — e ele está prontíssimo para receber profissionais com aquele algo a mais.

Os CV's permanecerão em poder da empresa enquanto perdurar o processo seletivo e pelo período adicional de 6 meses, para eventuais processos seletivos futuros, em atendimento a Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados.
PRINCIPAIS ATIVIDADES: Profissional com perfil operacional que atua na sustentação, monitoramento e resposta no dia a dia da segurança em nuvem pública AWS, garantindo a implementação, a operação contínua e a resiliência (SRE) dos controles de segurança em tecnologias, produtos e serviços de nuvem. Atua de forma colaborativa com os arquitetos de nuvem e com as demais equipes técnicas, próprias e contratadas, para operar a infraestrutura e os serviços de segurança em nuvem pública segundo os padrões, requisitos e melhores práticas de uso dos recursos.
  • Operar e sustentar no dia a dia os controles e ferramentas de segurança em nuvem pública AWS, garantindo o funcionamento contínuo de recursos como GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS WAF, Amazon Inspector, AWS Config e CloudTrail, com registro das atividades e cumprimento dos níveis de serviço acordados;
  • Monitorar de forma contínua os eventos e alertas de segurança, realizando triagem, priorização e encaminhamento das ocorrências, e atuando na abertura e no acompanhamento dos chamados relacionados;
  • Executar as atividades de resposta a incidentes de segurança, atuando na contenção, na investigação e na recuperação, além de documentar as ações e as lições aprendidas;
  • Conduzir a gestão operacional de vulnerabilidades, executando varreduras, triagem dos achados e acompanhamento das remediações junto às equipes responsáveis;
  • Aplicar e manter baselines e hardening de segurança em recursos de nuvem pública e ambientes on premise, seguindo benchmarks como CIS e as políticas internas do cliente;
  • Operar os mecanismos de gestão de identidade e acesso da AWS (IAM), apoiando a revisão de permissões, a rotação de credenciais e a aplicação do princípio do menor privilégio;
  • Analisar logs e trilhas de auditoria para identificar anomalias, apoiar investigações e sustentar as evidências de conformidade;
  • Apoiar a aplicação de patches e ajustes de configuração de segurança, mantendo os ambientes atualizados e em conformidade;
  • Atuar em conjunto com as demais equipes técnicas na integração das ferramentas de segurança aos processos de infraestrutura e DevOps, segundo práticas ITIL, agile e DevSecOps;
  • Documentar procedimentos operacionais, registrar as atividades executadas e manter atualizada a base de conhecimento da operação de segurança.

Graduação em área de Tecnologia da informação, ou qualquer curso de nível superior acompanhado de Pós-graduação na área de Tecnologia da Informação de no mínimo 360 (trezentos e sessenta) horas, em curso reconhecido pelo MEC.

Experiência prática em operação e sustentação de segurança em nuvem pública AWS (SecOps), incluindo monitoramento, resposta a incidentes e gestão de vulnerabilidades no dia a dia; Vivência com operação de serviços de segurança nativos da AWS, tais como GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, Amazon Inspector, AWS Config, CloudTrail, Amazon Detective e Amazon Macie; Experiência com SIEM, EDR/XDR, WAF, IDS/IPS, Patch Management, hardening e gestão de identidade e acesso; Vivência prática na aplicação dos frameworks de segurança do dia a dia, mapeando controles e evidências para NIST, CIS, MITRE ATT&CK, ISO 27001 e OWASP Top 10; Experiência técnica em gerenciamento de atividades segundo princípios e práticas ágeis, incluindo Manifesto Ágil, Scrum, Extreme Programming (XP) e Kanban; Experiência com práticas de DevSecOps aplicadas à rotina de integração, operação e segurança de sistemas e infraestrutura em nuvem pública e ambientes on premise; Vivência com segurança defensiva (Blue Team), threat hunting, análise de eventos e operação de SOC são um diferencial.
Conhecimento comprovado dos principais frameworks e boas práticas de segurança, com capacidade de aplicá-los na operação: MITRE ATT&CK e D3FEND, NIST, CIS Controls e CIS Benchmarks, ISO 27001 e OWASP Top 10.

jobs.description:
About OptimaFI

OptimaFI helps community financial institutions (CFIs) - credit unions and banks profitably grow using a combination of proven data assets, expert consulting, and modern cloud software. We are OptimaFI, striving to create solutions for CFI’s that enable better decision making, transparency, and improved profitability for our clients. Our values are Curiosity, Transparency, Partnership, and Lagniappe - always adding a little extra for clients and colleagues alike. We are an 80-person company growing to 100 in the next 18 months, and we have no intention of ballooning headcount for the sake of it. We move with purpose, invest in what works, and use automation and AI to stay lean and effective.

The Opportunity

OptimaFI already serves a meaningful share of the community financial institution market across software and services. This role is about accelerating software revenue with an experienced seller who can create pipelines, grow existing relationships, and close business across the portfolio. You own the territory and the work required to make it productive.

You will sell to banks and credit unions where reputation matters, and the market is finite. That means relevant outreach, strong discovery, and disciplined follow-through. Find the right institution, understand the need, connect it to the right solution, and keep the deal moving.

Key Responsibilities

  • Create the pipeline. Prospect through account research, direct outreach, relationships, referrals, events, and the existing client base. Be able to show what you personally created.
  • Own the territory. Build software revenue across both net-new institutions and current OptimaFI clients. Know where the best opportunities are and why.
  • Run strong discovery. Understand the institution's stated needs, connect it to the right solution, and know when to bring in a technical specialist.
  • Move the deal. Set clear next steps, maintain momentum, navigate objections and procurement, and carry qualified opportunities through close.
  • Keep the forecast real. Maintain accurate stages, buyer contacts, timing, next steps, and close dates in Salesforce. Requalify or close what is not moving.
  • Open doors for services. Identify qualified service needs and hand them to the right Services seller with the buyer need, context, and next step intact.
  • Help us learn. Record why opportunities advanced, stalled, were won, or were lost. Patterns should improve how we sell, demo, position, and build.

Required Qualifications

  • You've carried a real software sales number. You can walk us through quota, attainment, average deal size, sales cycle, and what you personally sourced.
  • You're a hunter. You have created meaningful pipeline without relying primarily on SDRs, BDRs, or Marketing to hand you opportunities.
  • You've done both. New-logo selling and expansion inside existing accounts. This is not an account-management-only seat.
  • You can own a complex sale. You lead discovery and the buyer relationship, use specialists for depth, and do not disappear when the conversation gets technical.
  • You can learn a portfolio. You are comfortable selling more than one product and translating technical or financial concepts into a clear business conversation.
  • You've sold into a market where trust matters. You understand that disciplined, relevant outreach beats noise.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Financial institution experience. Community banking, credit unions, fintech, financial software, payments, credit risk, finance, or another regulated B2B environment will help you ramp faster.
  • Experience in change. You have sold in a startup, scale-up, PE-backed, or evolving company where the process and support structure were not fully built for you.

You'll Thrive in This Role If You:

  • Create your own momentum. You do not wait for perfect leads, perfect tools, or perfect timing.
  • Ask good questions before pitching. You care more about relevance than reciting features.
  • Own the next step. You make it easy for buyers and internal partners to know what happens next.
  • Use experts well. You know when to bring in Solutions Consulting / Sales Engineering without handing away ownership of the deal.
  • Say what is happening. You communicate clearly when an opportunity is real, stuck, or unlikely to close.

Why OptimaFI

  • A meaningful market to sell into. OptimaFI has an established financial-institution client base and a broader software portfolio we are actively bringing to market.
  • Real ownership. This is a senior territory role with room to hunt, expand relationships, and shape how we sell.
  • Strong specialist support. You will have access to Solutions Consulting / Sales Engineering, Product, and banking SMEs without losing ownership of the sale.
  • A remote environment. We trust adults to do excellent work and expect clear ownership, transparency, and follow-through.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Client Engagement
jobs.excerpt: The Senior Director of Client Engagement is a strategic client and professional services leadership role at CampusWorks responsible for the successful delivery and client outcomes of a portfolio of professional services engagements.
jobs.description:
The Senior Director of Client Engagement is a strategic client and professional services leadership role at CampusWorks responsible for the successful delivery and client outcomes of a portfolio of professional services engagements. Reporting to the Vice President of Client Engagement, the Senior Director serves as the primary point of contact for professional services delivery within assigned client accounts and is accountable for delivery excellence, client satisfaction, trusted client relationships, forecast accuracy, timely revenue recognition, and on-time and on-budget project completion.

The Senior Director leads professional services engagements from initiation through completion, including workplan development, project oversight, client alignment, engagement economics, and direction of assigned project teams. Consultants assigned to engagements are formally managed within the Services organization; however, the Senior Director directs their work on assigned engagements and provides timely and substantive feedback regarding their performance.

The Senior Director works closely with Resource Management, Services, Client Engagement leadership, and Commercial teams to ensure engagements are appropriately staffed, client commitments are achieved, risks are addressed, and opportunities for additional client value are identified. In collaboration with the Vice President of Client Engagement, the Senior Director supports account strategy and builds strong relationships across assigned clients.

This position requires strong professional services delivery experience, sound business and financial judgment, executive-level client relationship skills, and the ability to lead effectively across a matrixed organization. This position will be 35% billable.

Essential Job Duties:

    Client Engagement Leadership:

    • Own the successful delivery of professional services projects and interim leader engagements within assigned accounts, ensuring contracted services, deliverables, quality standards, timelines, and expected client outcomes are achieved.
    • Lead all aspects of engagement initiation, including transition from contract to delivery, workplan development, project launch, establishment of delivery expectations, and coordination of assigned resources.
    • Develop and maintain clear, actionable workplans aligned with the statement of work, client priorities, project milestones, resource requirements, and expected outcomes.
    • Define engagement resource requirements and collaborate with Resource Management and Services leadership to identify appropriate resources and make adjustments as client or project needs change.
    • Orient, lead, and coach assigned project teams throughout the engagement, providing clear direction regarding project objectives, client expectations, deliverables, schedules, and work quality.
    • Monitor engagement performance, milestones, deliverables, risks, dependencies, and client issues and take timely action to keep projects progressing toward expected outcomes.
    • Identify and address project delays, scope concerns, client dependencies, resource issues, and other conditions that may affect successful delivery.
    • Manage project closeout, including confirming completion of contracted outcomes, capturing lessons learned, and identifying opportunities to improve future delivery.
    • Manage a portfolio of concurrent client engagements while appropriately balancing client priorities, project complexity, delivery risk, and organizational commitments.

      • Client Relationship Management:

      • Serve as the primary point of contact for client stakeholders regarding professional services delivery within assigned accounts.
      • Build trusted relationships with client sponsors, executives, project leaders, and other stakeholders through regular communication, sound judgment, responsiveness, and a clear understanding of institutional priorities.
      • Lead regular client meetings and project reviews to communicate progress, confirm priorities, gather feedback, address concerns, and maintain alignment between client expectations and contracted services.
      • Understand clients' evolving needs and challenges and adjust engagement plans, within the boundaries of the contracted scope, to ensure work remains relevant and produces meaningful outcomes.
      • Help clients resolve barriers that may delay project progress, decisions, access to information, or achievement of expected outcomes.
      • Review project deliverables and work products to ensure they meet client expectations, demonstrate appropriate quality, and clearly communicate the impact and value of the work.
      • Act as a trusted advisor by helping client leaders connect project activities and recommendations to their broader institutional goals.

        • Project Team Leadership and Performance:

        • Direct the work of consultants assigned to professional services engagements in alignment with the statement of work, project plan, client expectations, and CampusWorks standards.
        • Establish clear expectations for assigned project team members regarding responsibilities, deliverables, deadlines, client interaction, communication, and work quality.
        • Maintain regular communication with project team members to monitor progress, resolve barriers, ensure accountability, and support successful project delivery.
        • Provide timely, candid, and substantive performance feedback regarding assigned consultants to the appropriate Services leader for employees and Resource Management for independent contractors.
        • Promptly identify performance, capability, availability, or fit concerns that may affect engagement outcomes and work with Services and Resource Management leadership to determine appropriate action.
        • Partner with Services leadership regarding consultant capability and readiness while recognizing that formal supervision, professional development, and employee performance management reside within the Services organization.
        • Participate, as appropriate, in the identification, interviewing, and selection of consultants needed to meet specific client or engagement requirements.

          • Engagement Economics, Forecasting, and Resource Utilization:

          • Manage the financial performance of assigned engagements within the levers available to Client Engagement, with a focus on timely revenue recognition, accurate forecasting, delivery efficiency, scope management, and gross margin performance.
          • Ensure engagements begin promptly and effectively following contract execution so that delivery and revenue recognition are not unnecessarily delayed.
          • Maintain accurate engagement workplans and forecasts and proactively manage conditions that may create revenue or delivery variance.
          • Monitor assigned consulting hours against the workplan and collaborate with project teams, clients, Resource Management, and Services leadership to address significant variances.
          • Manage project-specific utilization of assigned resources by ensuring consultant time is aligned with planned work, client availability, engagement milestones, and evolving project requirements.
          • Protect engagement economics by actively managing scope, avoiding unnecessary non-billable activity, monitoring travel and other project expenses, and promoting efficient delivery.
          • Identify opportunities to deliver contracted outcomes more efficiently while maintaining quality, client satisfaction, and the integrity of the engagement.
          • Monitor gross margin performance against expectations established at contract signing and proactively identify and communicate risks that may affect financial performance.

            • Client Growth and Business Development Support:

            • Listen for emerging client challenges, priorities, and unmet needs during normal delivery activities and identify opportunities where CampusWorks may be able to provide additional value.
            • Communicate qualified business development leads and client needs promptly to the appropriate Client Engagement or Commercial leader.
            • Provide delivery expertise, client context, and subject matter support to Client Engagement and Commercial teams as they evaluate potential opportunities.
            • Participate in client meetings, proposal development, finalist presentations, solution design, and other business development activities when delivery or subject matter expertise is needed.
            • Support account strategy in partnership with the Vice President of Client Engagement by providing insight into client priorities, organizational dynamics, project outcomes, emerging risks, and potential areas of future need.
            • Maintain appropriate separation between delivery leadership and commercial ownership. The Senior Director identifies and supports opportunities but does not own commercial negotiations, Salesforce opportunity management, contracting, or booking.

              • Portfolio and Service Improvement:

              • Identify recurring delivery challenges, client needs, project risks, and successful practices across assigned engagements and share those insights with appropriate Client Engagement, Services, and organizational leaders.
              • Use project outcomes, client feedback, and lessons learned to recommend improvements to service delivery, engagement practices, tools, and supporting processes.
              • Contribute practical client and delivery insight to the continued evolution of CampusWorks' professional services offerings.
              • Collaborate across Client Engagement, Services, Resource Management, Commercial, and other functions to improve client outcomes while maintaining clear functional accountabilities.
              • Represent client and engagement needs in cross-functional discussions and proactively surface risks when organizational dependencies may affect client commitments.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Travel to client sites, as needed
  • Other duties, as assigned.

Required Skills/Abilities:

    • Demonstrated ability to lead and direct matrixed project teams, including consultants who do not directly report to the position.
    • Demonstrated ability to provide clear direction, candid performance feedback, and effective coaching in a professional services environment.
    • Experience managing senior-level client relationships and working directly with executives and other institutional decision-makers.
    • Strong business and financial acumen, including understanding of professional services revenue, utilization, project economics, forecasting, scope management, and gross margin.
    • Demonstrated ability to identify client needs and business opportunities while maintaining appropriate boundaries between professional services delivery and commercial ownership.
    • Strong understanding of higher education trends, challenges, operating environments, and opportunities strongly preferred.
    • Experience leading transformation initiatives within higher education or similarly complex organizations preferred.
    • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, and executive communication skills.
    • Strong judgment and the ability to navigate competing priorities, organizational dependencies, resource constraints, and complex client situations.
    • Demonstrated ability to work effectively across organizational boundaries and achieve results through collaboration, influence, clear accountability, and timely escalation.
    • Strategic and results-oriented mindset with the ability to connect project execution to client outcomes, organizational performance, and long-term client value.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree, in a related field.
  • 5+ years professional services, consulting, project/program delivery, or comparable client-services leadership experience, including responsibility for multiple concurrent client engagements.
  • 5+ years experience working in higher education or in an organization serving higher education institutions.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and managing project workplans, schedules, deliverables, risks, budgets, forecasts, and engagement economics.

Preferred Qualifications:

    • 10+ years of progressively responsible professional services, consulting, client engagement, or higher education leadership experience.
    • Experience leading transformation initiatives within higher education or similarly complex organizations.

What You Can Expect from Us

At CampusWorks, we don't just help our clients succeed; we help our employees succeed. Competitive pay, robust benefits for full-time employees, and professional development opportunities are a few of the many reasons that CampusWorks is a great place to build your career.

Our employees enjoy:

Meaningful work. Our employees often tell us that their work gives them a sense of purpose because it makes a difference in the lives of students and educators. CampusWorks Inc., as a large consulting firm,  provides its employees with an opportunity to work both onsite and remotely with our clients across the United States and in Canada.  With the nature of our clients’ work evolving quickly,  we’re all being asked to support larger CampusWorks initiatives. Upon joining CampusWorks in a consulting role, your talent and expertise may be applied to a range of projects, assignments, and clients. 

A virtual and onsite workplace. In an effort to reduce our environmental footprint, CampusWorks became a virtual company in 2012. As such, our team members are located across the U.S. and Canada, where they work from their home offices and at client sites.

Flexibility. We value work-life balance because we know that happy employees create happy customers. That's why CampusWorks offers both full-time and part-time 1099 consulting career opportunities to fit life's unique demands.

A company that gives back. Every year CampusWorks proudly supports numerous charitable fundraising initiatives that align with our vision to make higher education accessible to everyone.

 At CampusWorks, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives each CampusWorker (we call ourselves CampusWorkers) brings to our workplace each day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements. Founded in 1999, CampusWorks is dedicated to helping higher education overcome business and technological challenges that stand in the way of student success and completion. Our services are rooted in systems thinking and reach across the institution—from Student Services to Human Resources to Finance to Academics—to achieve transformative results.

Why This Role Matters?

As a Senior Cloud Infrastructure & Platform Engineer at Cint, you will directly shape the core foundation that powers our global research technology marketplace. Our platform processes real-time data from nearly 300 million respondents across 150 countries.

In this role, you will lead our primary technical OKR: modernizing our deployment ecosystem by migrating core workloads from Jenkins to Harness, while automating AWS infrastructure and empowering our R&D software teams with high-speed, self-service developer tooling.

What You Will Be Doing (Main Responsibilities):

  • CI/CD Modernization & Platform Migration: Spearhead our core business OKR of transitioning our continuous integration and delivery pipelines from legacy Jenkins to Harness. Automate software builds and deployments to eliminate repetitive manual operational overhead across R&D.
  • Infrastructure as Code & AWS Cloud Automation: Design, provision, and maintain high-availability AWS infrastructure (EKS, RDS, S3, ElastiCache) using modular Terraform, Docker, and Kubernetes. Ensure 100% Infrastructure-as-Code compliance across all platforms.
  • Developer Enablement & Internal Support: Serve as an embedded infrastructure expert supporting application development teams. Assist software engineers through our dedicated "Ask Infrastructure" channel, troubleshooting deployment issues, upgrading dependencies, and embedding DevOps culture across engineering scrums.
  • Observability, SRE & Incident Management : Enhance system telemetry and alerting across Grafana, Prometheus, and the ELK stack. Participate in an on-call rotation to maintain platform availability, with a structured 3-month onboarding runway before joining the active schedule.

What You Bring to the Role:

  • Cloud & Infrastructure as Code: Proven track record running production systems on AWS via CLI/API and building modular infrastructure using Terraform.
  • Containers & Orchestration: Strong practical experience with Docker containerization and Kubernetes management (EKS).
  • CI/CD & Automation: Deep understanding of the software development lifecycle, Git workflows, and build/release automation using Jenkins, Harness, or GitHub Actions.
  • Scripting & Tooling: Proficiency in at least one scripting or programming language (Python, Go, or Bash) for infrastructure automation.

Nice-to-Haves:

  • Direct experience with Harness CI/CD platform migrations.
  • Familiarity with multi-cloud architectures (GCP/Azure).
  • Experience configuring Grafana, Prometheus, or ELK telemetry stacks.

Our Values

Collaboration is our superpower

  • We uncover rich perspectives across the world
  • Success happens together
  • We deliver across borders.

Innovation is in our blood

  • We’re pioneers in our industry
  • Our curiosity is insatiable
  • We bring the best ideas to life.

We do what we say

  • We’re accountable for our work and actions
  • Excellence comes as standard
  • We’re open, honest and kind, always.

We are caring

  • We learn from each other’s experiences
  • Stop and listen; every opinion matters
  • We embrace diversity, equity and inclusion.

More About Cint

We’re proud to be recognised in Newsweek’s 2025 Global Top 100 Most Loved Workplaces®, reflecting our commitment to a culture of trust, respect, and employee growth.

In June 2021, Cint acquired Berlin-based GapFish – the world’s largest ISO certified online panel community in the DACH region – and in January 2022, completed the acquisition of US-based Lucid – a programmatic research technology platform that provides access to first-party survey data in over 110 countries.

Cint Group AB (publ), listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, this growth has made Cint a strong global platform with teams across its many global offices, including Stockholm, London, New York, New Orleans, Singapore, Tokyo and Sydney. (www.cint.com)

Additionally, in a world of AI, we want our candidates to understand our approach to the use of AI during the interview and hiring process, so we'd appreciate you reading our AI usage guide.

Who We Are

Cint is a pioneer in research technology (ResTech). Our customers use the Cint platform to post questions and get answers from real people to build business strategies, confidently publish research, accurately measure the impact of digital advertising, and more. The Cint platform is built on a programmatic marketplace, which is the world’s largest, with nearly 300 million respondents in over 150 countries who consent to sharing their opinions, motivations, and behaviours.

We are feeding the world’s curiosity!
